message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to launch a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that has an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and runs Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  
The example uses the **gcloud CLI** (the easiest way to interact with the Compute Engine API).  
If you prefer to call the REST API directly, the same parameters are shown in the JSON payload at the end.

> **Prerequisites**  
> * You have a Google Cloud project (`PROJECT_ID`) with billing enabled.  
> * The Compute Engine API is enabled (`gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com`).  
> * You have the `gcloud` CLI installed and authenticated (`gcloud auth login`).  
> * You have the **NVIDIA GPU driver** installed on the instance (see the post‑creation script below).  
> * You have a **service account** or user with the `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1` role (or equivalent).  

---

## 1. Create the instance with `gcloud`

```bash
# Variables – replace with your own values
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"          # pick a zone that supports GPUs
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8" # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM – adjust as needed
GPU_COUNT=1
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-tesla-a6000"
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
  --accelerator=type="$GPU_TYPE,count=$GPU_COUNT" \
  --image-family="$IMAGE_FAMILY" \
  --image-project="$IMAGE_PROJECT" \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
  --tags=http-server,https-server \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform
```

### Explanation of key flags

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--accelerator` | Attaches the specified GPU(s). |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Uses the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image. |
| `--boot-disk-size` | Gives the VM enough space for the OS, drivers, and your workloads. |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh` | Runs a shell script after boot to install the NVIDIA driver and CUDA toolkit. |
| `--tags` | Allows HTTP/HTTPS traffic if you plan to expose a web service. |
| `--scopes` | Grants the VM full Cloud Platform access (adjust scopes if you need tighter security). |

---

## 2. `startup.sh` – install NVIDIA driver & CUDA

Create a file named `startup.sh` in the same directory as the `gcloud` command:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -e

# Update package lists
apt-get update

# Install prerequisites
apt-get install -y build-essential dkms

# Add NVIDIA package repositories
wget https://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/repos/ubuntu2004/x86_64/cuda-ubuntu2004.pin
mv cuda-ubuntu2004.pin /etc/apt/preferences.d/cuda-repository-pin-600
wget https://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/12.2.0/local_installers/cuda-repo-ubuntu2004-12-2-local_12.2.0-535.54.03-1_amd64.deb
dpkg -i cuda-repo-ubuntu2004-12-2-local_12.2.0-535.54.03-1_amd64.deb
apt-key add /var/cuda-repo-ubuntu2004-12-2-local/7fa2af80.pub
apt-get update

# Install NVIDIA driver and CUDA toolkit
apt-get install -y cuda-drivers
apt-get install -y cuda-toolkit-12-2

# Verify installation
nvidia-smi
```

> **Tip:** If you only need the driver (no CUDA), replace the `cuda-toolkit-12-2` line with `nvidia-driver-535`.

Make sure the script is executable:

```bash
chmod +x startup.sh
```

---

## 3. Verify the instance

After the instance boots, SSH into it:

```bash
gcloud compute ssh "$INSTANCE_NAME" --zone="$ZONE"
```

Once logged in, run:

```bash
nvidia-smi
```

You should see something like:

```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 535.54.03    Driver Version: 535.54.03    CUDA Version: 12.2     |
|-------------------------------+----------------------+----------------------+
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
| Fan  Temp  Perf  Pwr:Usage/Cap|         Memory-Usage | GPU-Util  Compute M. |
|                               |                      |               MIG M. |
|===============================+======================+======================|
|   0  NVIDIA RTX A6000     Off | 00000000:01:00.0 Off |                  N/A |
|  0%   35C    P8    15W / 300W |      0MiB / 16384MiB |      0%      Default |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

---

## 4. REST API equivalent (JSON payload)

If you prefer to use the Compute Engine REST API directly, the following JSON can be POSTed to:

```
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/instances
```

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y build-essential dkms\n# ... (rest of the script above) ..."
      }
    ]
  },
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  },
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

> Replace `my-gcp-project` and `us-central1-a` with your actual project ID and zone.  
> The `startup-script` value can be base64‑encoded if you prefer to keep it short.

---

## 5. Clean up

When you’re done, delete the instance to avoid incurring charges:

```bash
gcloud compute instances delete "$INSTANCE_NAME" --zone="$ZONE" --quiet
```

---

### Quick Reference

| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `gcloud compute instances create …` | Launch instance with GPU |
| `startup.sh` | Installs NVIDIA driver & CUDA |
| `nvidia-smi` | Verify GPU availability |
| `gcloud compute instances delete …` | Clean up resources |

Feel free to tweak the machine type, GPU count, or disk size to match your workload. Happy GPU computing!
